biomarkers.name: SF-1 (steroidogenic factor 1)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Distinguishes adrenal cortical neoplasms from RCC and many other adrenal/retroperitoneal masses

biomarkers.name: Ki-67
biomarkers.clinical_use: Not a component of the original Weiss score; often used as an adjunct in distinguishing adenoma from carcinoma and is a major prognostic marker (higher = worse). A cutoff around >5% supports malignancy in indeterminate cases, and Ki-67 is incorporated into grading/prognostic stratification

biomarkers.name: TP53 (germline)
biomarkers.prevalence: Li-Fraumeni syndrome association; enriched in paediatric ACC, with very high prevalence in southern Brazilian paediatric series due to founder TP53 p.R337H

biomarkers.name: CTNNB1 (b2-catenin)
biomarkers.clinical_use: WNT/b2-catenin pathway activation is common and is associated with adverse biology/prognosis

biomarkers.name: IGF2 overexpression
biomarkers.clinical_use: Very common molecular hallmark in ACC; related to 11p15 alterations/loss of imprinting. Target of prior IGF-axis therapeutic trials

biomarkers.name: Serum steroids (cortisol, DHEA-S, aldosterone, sex steroids)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Establish functional status (Cushing syndrome, androgen excess/virilisation, less often aldosterone or estrogen excess). Cortisol excess is associated with worse prognosis. Steroid profiles by mass spectrometry are emerging

biomarkers.name: Urinary steroid metabolomics (24h urine or LC-MS)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Emerging diagnostic tool differentiating ACC from adenoma

biomarkers.name: MSI / dMMR
biomarkers.prevalence: Rare in sporadic ACC; Lynch-associated cases exist

biomarkers.name: ZNRF3
biomarkers.clinical_use: Recurrent ACC driver affecting WNT signaling; part of the molecular hallmark landscape

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Nests, trabeculae, or diffuse sheets of polygonal cells with eosinophilic to clear cytoplasm; nuclear atypia, mitoses, capsular/vascular invasion
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Weiss criteria (3 of 9 features supports malignancy); ENSAT stage; Ki-67 is the main proliferation-based prognostic marker and is used in grading/prognostic stratification, although cutoffs vary across studies and guidelines

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Immune-cold typically; hypercortisolism in functional tumours further suppresses immune infiltrate
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Delicate fibrovascular stroma; extensive necrosis in high-grade tumours

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Adrenal cortical cells (zona fasciculata, glomerulosa, or reticularis)
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Mesoderm  intermediate mesoderm (adrenal cortex from urogenital ridge, distinct from neural crest-derived medulla)
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Retains steroidogenic differentiation (inhibin+, SF-1+, calretinin+, Melan-A+/MART-1+); often produces steroid hormones (most commonly cortisol and/or androgens, less often aldosterone or oestrogens) driving clinical syndromes
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Transcriptomic subtypes reflect biologically distinct states, including more proliferative/aggressive groups with dedifferentiation; WNT/b2-catenin activation is a major subset. TP53 alterations are common in aggressive disease; ATRX alterations are reported but are not established as the defining driver of the most aggressive subset
